name: single call
intent: Execute one direct language model inference without branching loops or external tool iterations when a single pass suffices.
structure: Input payload and system prompt pass once to the model, optionally validating a structured schema before returning the output.
when_to_use: Use when tasks involve classification, extraction, translation, or concise drafting over context already available in full.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when tasks require live lookups, multi-step verification, or recovering from runtime errors.
tradeoffs: Lowest possible latency and predictable cost in exchange for zero external verification or dynamic exploration.
example: Categorizing an inbound support ticket into priority tier and billing topic in one structured response.

name: prompt chaining
intent: Decompose a complex transformation into a fixed linear sequence of focused model calls paired with programmatic gates.
structure: Each stage executes one prompt over the previous stage output, running deterministic schema or sanity checks between links.
when_to_use: Use when subtasks decompose naturally into sequential stages where checking intermediate steps prevents downstream drift.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when dynamic open-ended branching is required or sequential latency exceeds interactive response budgets.
tradeoffs: Raises accuracy per stage and simplifies debugging at the expense of serialized multi-call latency.
example: Translating a technical policy specification into structured clause tables and then validating completeness checks.

name: routing
intent: Classify each incoming query or intermediate signal and dispatch execution to a specialized downstream prompt, workflow, or model.
structure: An entry router inspects intent, language, complexity, or policy sensitivity and invokes only the matched handler branch.
when_to_use: Use when user inputs span distinct problem classes whose specialized instructions or models would degrade if merged together.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when routing criteria overlap ambiguously without clear fallback handlers.
tradeoffs: Keeps specialized prompts lean and optimizes model cost per difficulty while introducing router misclassification risk.
example: Sending simple FAQ questions directly to compact cached pipelines while routing refund disputes to policy workflows.

name: parallelization
intent: Run independent subtask calls or guardrail checks concurrently and aggregate results once parallel branches complete.
structure: Workflow fan-out dispatches isolated sectioning or voting tasks simultaneously across worker invocations before a merge barrier.
when_to_use: Use when work splits cleanly into independent document sections, parallel source queries, or distinct guardrail evaluations.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when sequential state dependencies require inspecting step output before initiating the next action.
tradeoffs: Significantly reduces wall-clock waiting time while concentrating peak request bursts and rate-limit load.
example: Executing separate PII redaction, compliance policy checks, and customer lookup queries at the same time.

name: orchestrator-workers
intent: Delegate dynamically determined subtasks from a central orchestrator model to specialized worker agents and synthesize their findings.
structure: The orchestrator plans work at runtime, dispatches scoped briefs to stateless or isolated workers, collects summaries, and produces the final artifact.
when_to_use: Use when subtask count and required specializations cannot be hardcoded ahead of time, such as repository refactoring or deep research.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when workflow steps are fixed upfront and simple chaining achieves the same outcome faster.
tradeoffs: Handles unpredictable multi-file or multi-source problems cleanly while risking coordination overhead if task boundaries blur.
example: A coding lead agent reading an issue, assigning test inspection and patch authoring to worker agents, and verifying tests.

name: evaluator-optimizer
intent: Pair a generator call with a separate evaluator critic loop that scores drafts against explicit criteria until quality passes or limits trigger.
structure: Generator produces a candidate output, evaluator inspects it against rubrics or deterministic checks, and concrete critique triggers refinement.
when_to_use: Use when clear evaluation criteria exist and iterative refinement measurably improves translation, code correctness, or rubric fidelity.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when objective rubric checks are missing or latency targets preclude repeated revision rounds.
tradeoffs: Substantially raises output polish and adherence at the cost of multiplied token expense and bounded extra turns.
example: Generating legal risk summaries followed by a compliance critic flagging uncited assertions before delivery.

name: tool-calling loop
intent: Allow a model to invoke external registered tools iteratively, observe returned payloads, and continue looping until producing a final response.
structure: Host submits prompt and JSON tool definitions, executes model-selected calls safely, appends tool outputs to turn history, and repeats within turn caps.
when_to_use: Use when tasks need live data retrieval, calculations, database lookups, or transactional API calls decided dynamically by context.
when_not_to_use: Avoid granting unrestricted loops without strict step budgets, parameter schemas, and timeout guards.
tradeoffs: Unlocks real-world environment interaction while requiring defensive schema validation and context pruning per turn.
example: A DevOps triage loop checking service health metrics, fetching recent deployments, and querying error logs before diagnosing.

name: ReAct loop
intent: Alternate explicit reasoning thoughts, environment tool actions, and resulting observations inside an interpretable iterative cycle.
structure: Each cycle logs a brief rationale selecting the next action, runs the action, ingests observation text, and updates reasoning state.
when_to_use: Use when transparent multi-hop reasoning traces help humans audit why tools were called or recover cleanly from partial results.
when_not_to_use: Avoid redundant verbose thought prose on trivial lookup calls where plain tool invocation suffices.
tradeoffs: Improves step-level interpretability and reduces blind guesses while consuming additional reasoning tokens per cycle.
example: Investigating a cross-departmental discrepancy by reasoning about missing invoice numbers before each database query.

name: plan-and-execute
intent: Generate an explicit ordered multi-step plan first, then dispatch step execution sequentially or concurrently with optional replanning.
structure: A planner emits structured task milestones, worker steps execute them while updating state, and a replanner revises remaining steps if assumptions fail.
when_to_use: Use when complex multi-step objectives benefit from global dependency ordering, user plan review, and structured progress tracking.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when environments mutate unpredictably on every single action, rendering advance plans immediately stale.
tradeoffs: Clarifies scope upfront and prevents aimless looping while risking wasted planning effort if replanning happens constantly.
example: Drafting a structured travel itinerary skeleton, checking availability per booking segment, and revising alternatives upon conflicts.

name: reflection loop
intent: Capture execution failures, test traces, or critic verdicts and generate reflective diagnostics persisted across retries or episodes.
structure: Following an unsuccessful step or failing check, a reflection prompt summarizes causes and feeds concrete corrective guidance into the next attempt.
when_to_use: Use on coding, reasoning, and environment tasks equipped with objective error feedback such as compilers, linters, or tests.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when no external failure signal exists and self-reflection would hallucinate confidence over bad assumptions.
tradeoffs: Accelerates recovery from concrete execution errors while requiring strict retry ceilings to avoid infinite spin.
example: Reading failing pytest stack traces to diagnose an off-by-one bug and storing the lesson across candidate retries.

name: human approval gate
intent: Pause execution immediately before high-impact external side effects, checkpointing full state until an authorized operator approves or rejects.
structure: Pre-registered sensitive tool calls trigger a runtime interrupt surfacing exact action parameters and rationale to a human review queue.
when_to_use: Use for irreversible mutations such as external emails, financial transfers, production changes, deletion commands, or regulated decisions.
when_not_to_use: Avoid gating low-risk read-only queries where interruptions ruin responsiveness and cause reviewer fatigue.
tradeoffs: Prevents unauthorized or costly side effects at the cost of asynchronous human response latency.
example: Pausing an outbound vendor settlement workflow to verify invoice totals and bank details with finance staff.

name: fallback chain
intent: Configure ordered recovery paths across secondary models, simplified prompts, deterministic rules, or human handoff upon failures.
structure: Execution tries primary route with timeout and schema checks; rate limits, HTTP faults, or validation errors cascade automatically to backup handlers.
when_to_use: Use in latency-sensitive or business-critical deployments needing graceful degradation during provider outages or quota saturation.
when_not_to_use: Avoid routing high-risk actions onto unvetted weak fallback models without preserving full guardrail enforcement.
tradeoffs: Sustains high availability under upstream instability while requiring careful maintenance of secondary prompt compatibility.
example: Switching from a saturated primary provider endpoint cleanly to a secondary regional deployment or safe FAQ escalation.

name: map-reduce summarization
intent: Partition oversized documents into bounded chunks, summarize or extract insights in parallel (map), and merge findings hierarchically (reduce).
structure: Chunk processors transform segments independently into compact summaries combined iteratively by reducer calls up to target length.
when_to_use: Use when total input volume exceeds reliable effective context attention even inside large-window models.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when subtle holistic cross-section dependencies break completely across independent chunk boundaries.
tradeoffs: Scales cleanly over massive corpora with bounded attention noise while adding parallel token volume and boundary-splitting risk.
example: Analyzing lengthy earnings transcripts, anomaly log bundles, or security advisories chunk by chunk before final synthesis.

name: agentic RAG
intent: Embed retrieval inside an active agent loop so the model dynamically decides whether, how, and across which indices to query and refine searches.
structure: Instead of one blind top-K lookup, the agent rewrites queries, chooses tool backends, inspects returned snippets, and searches again if insufficient.
when_to_use: Use when user questions span multiple knowledge bases, require query reformulation, or mix structured lookups with unstructured docs.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when single deterministic semantic lookup already locates canonical policy passages quickly.
tradeoffs: Dramatically improves recall on ambiguous or multi-hop queries while raising latency and token variation.
example: Iteratively searching product documentation, changelogs, and ticket history until locating a root fix.

name: corrective RAG
intent: Score retrieved document relevance dynamically prior to generation, filtering bad chunks and triggering query rewrite or external search fallback on low confidence.
structure: A lightweight retrieval grader classifies hits into relevant, ambiguous, or irrelevant before either synthesizing, decomposing, or falling back.
when_to_use: Use when noisy vector indices frequently surface weakly relevant passages that tempt models into ungrounded answers.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when source repositories are trivially scoped and pre-filtered deterministically.
tradeoffs: Protects output faithfulness and avoids stale local gaps while adding one extra grading pass per retrieval.
example: Rejecting mismatched legacy policy snippets in HR onboarding chat and refining search terms with current department filters.

name: memory write-back
intent: Distill salient facts, resolved preferences, and session outcomes asynchronously or post-turn into long-term stores after conflict resolution.
structure: Dedicated extractors filter raw conversation logs, check similarity against stored facts, and issue explicit insert, merge, or delete mutations.
when_to_use: Use in ongoing personal assistants, coding companions, and recurring client agents where continuity across sessions adds value.
when_not_to_use: Avoid auto-saving untrusted third-party inputs directly into shared enterprise memory without verification.
tradeoffs: Creates adaptive long-term personalization while requiring careful deduplication, scoping, and poisoning defenses.
example: Saving a user's preferred currency, accessibility needs, or team repo conventions cleanly at session close.

name: supervisor
intent: Route turns repeatedly through a central supervisor agent that selects which specialized subagent acts next and checks overall completion.
structure: Workers report back exclusively to shared state inspected by the supervisor, which invokes handoff tools until all subtasks satisfy goals.
when_to_use: Use when multi-role coordination requires central policy oversight, shared global visibility, and flexible turn sequencing.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when simple fixed sequential pipelines work without adaptive routing overhead.
tradeoffs: Simplifies global authorization and quality checks around multi-agent teams while risking a central supervisor bottleneck.
example: A research supervisor directing data-gathering, statistical computation, and citation-checking specialists iteratively.

name: swarm handoff
intent: Let specialized peer agents transfer active user control and session context directly to another peer when domain boundaries shift.
structure: Each peer advertises handoff tools for adjacent specialists; invoking one passes current thread context cleanly and swaps system instructions.
when_to_use: Use in multi-domain customer workflows where direct agent-to-agent transfer preserves fluid user rapport without supervisor hops.
when_not_to_use: Avoid lacking loop detection or turn caps that would trap peer agents in reciprocal handoffs.
tradeoffs: Reduces central orchestration hops and keeps domain prompts focused while making end-to-end execution paths decentralized.
example: An automated order lookup agent transferring smoothly to a warranty claim specialist upon detecting damaged delivery items.

name: debate or critic
intent: Run structured peer critique across independent candidate solvers or opposing roles before a referee synthesizes a vetted conclusion.
structure: Multiple models draft independent analyses, examine peer rationales across bounded rounds, challenge unsupported claims, and vote or reconcile.
when_to_use: Use on high-consequence reasoning, planning, or research synthesis where single-model blind spots pose costly errors.
when_not_to_use: Avoid on routine latency-sensitive tasks where multiplied token usage outweighs marginal accuracy gains.
tradeoffs: Surfaces subtle flaws and conflicting assumptions while raising compute cost linearly per debater and round.
example: Evaluating architectural design proposals with separate security, scalability, and cost critic perspectives before sign-off.

name: guardrail wrapper
intent: Enclose model inferences and tool invocations inside pre-check and post-check validation middleware enforcing safety, PII, and schema rules.
structure: Input rails screen incoming text before model execution while output rails validate structure, secrets leakage, and policy bounds before release.
when_to_use: Use across external user-facing agents, regulated workflows, and multi-tool systems handling untrusted documents.
when_not_to_use: Avoid relying solely on regex wrapper checks without fixing underlying authorization or sandbox privileges.
tradeoffs: Establishes consistent centralized safety enforcement across diverse models while adding modest inspection latency.
example: Running prompt-injection screening on inbound emails and PII masking on outgoing customer support drafts.

name: sandboxed code execution
intent: Execute agent-generated code inside isolated microVMs or hardened ephemeral containers with strict timeouts, resource caps, and blocked egress.
structure: Code blocks pass into sandbox APIs rather than local host processes, returning bounded stdout, stderr, and generated artifacts cleanly.
when_to_use: Use whenever coding, data science, or custom analytics agents run dynamically synthesized scripts.
when_not_to_use: Avoid executing unverified generated scripts on shared application hosts or privileged build nodes.
tradeoffs: Eliminates arbitrary host compromise risk while adding container cold-start latency and image provisioning work.
example: Executing untrusted data transformation code in an isolated E2B microVM to compute financial charts safely.

name: structured output enforcement
intent: Bind model generations to explicit typed JSON Schemas using constrained decoding or typed retry validation before downstream consumption.
structure: Frameworks convert typed data classes into strict provider schemas and re-prompt automatically with validation diffs upon rare mismatches.
when_to_use: Use whenever downstream databases, ticket routers, extraction jobs, or tool hosts consume model fields programmatically.
when_not_to_use: Avoid asking for verbose unstructured markdown prose when strict field parsing is needed.
tradeoffs: Guarantees parseable machine contracts at the expense of slight schema-grammar constraints on expressive wording.
example: Enforcing typed insurance claim severity codes, entity IDs, and rationale strings via Pydantic validation.

name: episodic context compaction
intent: Compress completed dialogue segments and resolved tool observations into dense checkpoints before working context fills attention limits.
structure: Context managers track token thresholds, trigger structured summarization over aging turns, retain key constraints, and drop raw bloat.
when_to_use: Use in extended multi-turn support chats, debugging sessions, and persistent workspace assistants.
when_not_to_use: Avoid discarding exact active error traces or mandatory safety constraints during over-aggressive compression.
tradeoffs: Sustains long sessions within manageable latency and token budgets while risking subtle detail loss if badly summarized.
example: Compacting thirty resolved search and setup turns into a concise workspace summary while fixing build errors.

name: deliberative search and backtracking
intent: Explore multiple lookahead action branches over trees or graphs, evaluating intermediate states and pruning unpromising paths.
structure: Search algorithms such as Tree of Thoughts or LATS pair LLM action proposals with value functions and state restoration to backtrack.
when_to_use: Use on hard multi-step puzzles, program synthesis, or planning problems where greedy first steps frequently dead-end.
when_not_to_use: Avoid on routine conversational queries where multi-branch rollouts inflate response times unacceptably.
tradeoffs: Finds valid paths hidden from greedy decoding while multiplying inference token usage and execution complexity.
example: Testing multiple SQL join strategies in parallel states and backtracking cleanly when one hits cardinality timeouts.

name: dynamic tool selection
intent: Retrieve and bind only the relevant subset of tools from large catalogs per turn or task using semantic matching or permissions filtering.
structure: Instead of injecting hundreds of schemas into every prompt, a retrieval pre-step selects top task-matched tool definitions dynamically.
when_to_use: Use when agents integrate with massive SaaS suites, enterprise APIs, or large MCP server federations.
when_not_to_use: Avoid when total available tools fit comfortably inside clean compact schemas.
tradeoffs: Preserves context focus and shrinks prompt token waste while risking missed tools if retrieval metadata is poor.
example: Loading only GitHub and Jira schemas into context after intent detection identifies a bug-triage query.

name: hybrid memory retrieval
intent: Combine working session context, recent episodic logs, semantic vector facts, and knowledge graphs into unified memory queries per turn.
structure: Memory routers query multiple stores with recency, importance, and semantic relevance weighting before merging non-redundant facts into context.
when_to_use: Use in rich longitudinal assistants, healthcare admin continuity, or personalization agents tracking evolving user relationships.
when_not_to_use: Avoid complex hybrid memory wiring when stateless per-session workflows satisfy product requirements.
tradeoffs: Produces nuanced context-aware recall while demanding clean conflict resolution when stored facts evolve.
example: Combining current project files with prior episodic debug notes and team coding conventions at session start.

name: cited evidence synthesis
intent: Aggregate retrieved evidence across multiple documents while attaching exact claim-level source spans and inline provenance tags.
structure: Models receive numbered document excerpts with required schema constraints forcing every factual assertion to reference supporting passage IDs.
when_to_use: Use in legal research, academic literature reviews, compliance analysis, and verifiable customer policy assistants.
when_not_to_use: Avoid displaying unverified post-hoc links appended without checking span alignment.
tradeoffs: Makes every claim rapidly auditable for human reviewers while tightening generation flexibility.
example: Drafting a compliance gap memo where each finding links directly to specific regulatory article paragraphs.

name: hybrid search with reranking
intent: Fuse exact keyword matching with dense embedding retrieval, then apply a cross-encoder reranker to elevate top passages before generation.
structure: BM25 and vector queries execute in parallel, merge via reciprocal rank fusion, and pass top candidates through a neural reranker.
when_to_use: Use across technical knowledge bases containing exact API names, codes, identifiers, and conceptual explanations.
when_not_to_use: Avoid adding cross-encoder reranking latency on tiny single-document collections.
tradeoffs: Significantly raises retrieval precision across both literal and semantic queries while adding modest reranker inference cost.
example: Retrieving exact medical coding policy updates combining CPT identifier search with semantic descriptions.

name: hypothesis generation and critic
intent: Iteratively propose testable hypotheses from retrieved scientific or analytical data and challenge each hypothesis against counterfactual checks.
structure: A synthesizer proposes candidate explanations and evidence links while a skeptical critic probes edge cases, contradictions, and missing data.
when_to_use: Use in R&D exploration, root-cause diagnostics, fraud investigation, and strategic decision analysis.
when_not_to_use: Avoid presenting unverified speculative hypotheses to non-expert users without explicit uncertainty caveats.
tradeoffs: Promotes rigorous exploration beyond surface summaries while requiring strict grounding discipline to stay factual.
example: Evaluating competing hypotheses for intermittent manufacturing defects against telemetry logs and maintenance records.

name: automated judge verification
intent: Embed calibrated rubric-based model judges inside workflows or CI pipelines to score responses for faithfulness, completeness, and safety.
structure: Judge prompts inspect input context, generated output, and structured scoring rubrics, emitting pass flags or scalar critiques.
when_to_use: Use to gate releases, evaluate open-ended agent trajectories, and flag low-faithfulness production runs for human audit.
when_not_to_use: Avoid replacing deterministic programmatic tests with probabilistic LLM judges when exact assertions are possible.
tradeoffs: Scales qualitative quality auditing across thousands of interactions while requiring careful human calibration.
example: Scoring retrieved grounding and tone consistency automatically across multi-turn customer support eval runs.

name: action scope and policy enforcement
intent: Enforce deterministic authorization scopes, parameter bounds, spending caps, and environment allowlists externally at tool execution boundaries.
structure: Tool hosts validate caller credentials, OAuth scopes, schema limits, and domain allowlists prior to dispatching backend API calls.
when_to_use: Use across all agents holding financial, administrative, CRM, email, or external mutation tools.
when_not_to_use: Avoid delegating critical security or spending rules exclusively to prompt wording.
tradeoffs: Guarantees hard safety boundaries regardless of model errors while requiring explicit security policy maintenance.
example: Validating refund dollar thresholds and allowed customer ownership server-side before billing execution.

name: peer discovery and protocol delegation
intent: Discover external specialized agents via standardized Agent Cards or registries and delegate structured tasks asynchronously across network protocols.
structure: Clients inspect capability metadata, authenticate via OAuth or JWT, send typed A2A task requests, and stream progress artifacts.
when_to_use: Use when workflows cross organizational, cloud vendor, or team runtime boundaries.
when_not_to_use: Avoid introducing cross-network protocol overhead between closely coupled helper steps inside one process.
tradeoffs: Enables interoperable multi-vendor agent ecosystems while introducing distributed auth and network timeout management.
example: Delegating customs compliance verification from a logistics planner agent to a partner compliance agent over A2A.

name: procedural skill reuse
intent: Index verified successful execution trajectories and reusable workflow scripts into procedural libraries retrieved by task similarity.
structure: Upon completing a novel multi-step procedure cleanly, systems extract modular parameterized instructions or verified scripts for future lookup.
when_to_use: Use in embodied robotics, software automation, and repetitive operations workflows tackling recurring task families.
when_not_to_use: Avoid storing brittle fragile sequences tied to hardcoded transient IDs without validation checks.
tradeoffs: Reduces repeated exploration cost on familiar tasks while risking stale failures if external environments change.
example: Reusing a verified repository lint-and-release skill workflow stored after prior successful execution.

name: shared blackboard collaboration
intent: Coordinate multiple peer agents asynchronously through a shared structured workspace or message board where agents post partial findings and claim tasks.
structure: Agents read shared state artifacts, post intermediate analyses or critiques, resolve dependencies collaboratively, and finalize deliverables.
when_to_use: Use for open-ended collaborative investigation, cross-functional design review, or sharded parallel execution.
when_not_to_use: Avoid leaving concurrent state writes uncoordinated without schema locking or clear completion rules.
tradeoffs: Supports flexible emergent peer collaboration while demanding clear anti-duplication and convergence protocols.
example: Multiple worker agents analyzing separate dataset partitions and posting validated outputs onto a shared coordination board.

name: durable checkpointed execution
intent: Run long-horizon agent workflows atop durable engines that persist step outcomes, survive process restarts, and resume awaiting human or API events.
structure: Workflow runtimes journal completed LLM and tool calls deterministically, replaying prior results seamlessly without re-executing side effects after recovery.
when_to_use: Use for multi-hour code migrations, asynchronous approval workflows, incident investigations, and multi-day enterprise tasks.
when_not_to_use: Avoid adding heavyweight durable orchestration infrastructure to trivial sub-second stateless APIs.
tradeoffs: Delivers strong crash recovery and clean pause-and-resume semantics while requiring deterministic workflow boundaries.
example: Surviving server deployments gracefully mid-way through a multi-hour automated incident investigation and human review pause.
